This medication is contraindicated in individuals with known hypersensitivity to rifamycin or any other antimicrobial agents within the rifamycin class. 3. It is not effective for treating diarrhea that is complicated by fever and/or bloody stools. 4. If diarrhea worsens or persists for more than 48 hours, discontinue use and consider alternative antibacterial therapy. 5. Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea (CDAD) should be considered in all patients presenting with diarrhea following the use of antibacterial drugs. 6. CDAD can occur up to two months after discontinuation of antibiotic therapy. 7. Prescribing rifamycin without a confirmed or strongly suspected bacterial infection, or without a prophylactic indication, is unlikely to benefit the patient and increases the risk of developing drug-resistant bacteria. 8. Due to minimal systemic concentrations of rifamycin observed, clinically significant drug interactions are not expected. 9. There is no available data regarding the use of this medication in pregnant women. 10. Systemic absorption in humans is negligible following oral administration, and maternal use is not expected to result in fetal exposure. 11. There is no available data regarding the presence of this medication in human breast milk. 12. Systemic absorption in humans is negligible following oral administration, and exposure to breastfed infants through breast milk is expected to be negligible. 13. The developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding should be weighed against the mother’s clinical need for the drug and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed child or from the underlying maternal condition. 14. This medication is generally considered acceptable during pregnancy. Controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. 15. Approximately 1% of the drug is protein-bound, with about 80% of the drug bound to plasma proteins. 16. CYP-based metabolism has not been observed in vitro. 17. The drug is primarily excreted via feces, with 86% of the dose eliminated through this route. 18. Each dose should be taken with a full glass of liquid (6–8 ounces). 19. Do not take this medication concomitantly with alcohol. 20. It may be taken with or without food. 21. Swallow delayed-release tablets whole; do not crush, break, or chew them. 22.
